name: Michigan Dogman
description: A bipedal, dog-headed humanoid cryptid reported primarily in the northwestern Lower Peninsula of Michigan, popularized by a 1987 radio prank song by disc jockey Steve Cook of WTCM-FM in Traverse City.
full_description: The Michigan Dogman is a cryptid said to inhabit the forests of the northwestern Lower Peninsula of Michigan, particularly around Wexford, Manistee, and Cross Village. Witnesses describe a roughly seven-foot-tall bipedal creature with a man-like torso, fur, and the head of a dog or wolf, with blue or amber eyes and a vocalization sometimes likened to a human scream. The phenomenon entered popular awareness through 'The Legend', a song that disc jockey Steve Cook recorded as an April Fools' Day prank for WTCM-FM (Traverse City) in 1987. Cook has consistently described the song as fiction; nevertheless it generated more than a hundred reports from listeners and helped seed a regional folklore that was subsequently reinforced by media including MonsterQuest (2010) and the local feature film Dogman (2011). Investigative work by author Linda S. Godfrey, originally focused on Wisconsin's Beast of Bray Road, has since extended to Michigan and the wider Great Lakes region. Mainstream zoology does not recognize the Dogman; reports are typically attributed to misidentification, hoaxes, or the cultural transmission set in motion by Cook's song.
origin: Reports cluster in the northwestern Lower Peninsula of Michigan, particularly around the Manistee River and historically Odawa lands; occasional reports extend into other Great Lakes states.
